strings.records.gmo-domain-stop.title: GMO: individual contact begins for payments and alternatives; 428 tips
strings.records.gmo-domain-stop.body: At 15:30 on 10/30, GMO announced that direct contact had begun about condolence-payment procedures and alternative services. Notice16 records 428 cumulative tips at 18:00 that day. Tips do not count victims or arrests; completed payments and service recovery remain unconfirmed.
strings.records.gmo-domain-stop.action: Use official individual contact to confirm procedures, alternative services and compensation conditions. Reject opportunistic requests for credentials or fees.
strings.records.gmo-domain-stop.time: 10/30 15:30 and 18:00 JST / Prior-source context; body not fully re-reviewed in this update
strings.records.atlink-beta.title: @link: beta testing at some medical institutions, not full resumption.
strings.records.atlink-beta.body: The 10/28 12:30 update describes the start of cloud beta testing at some medical institutions. Patient apps, web reservations, and external-system integrations remain suspended. Effects on medical institutions' reservation operations continue, and the number of records affected by leakage remains under investigation.
strings.records.atlink-beta.action: Contact your medical institution directly about reservations or changes. Distinguish planned resumptions/refunds from completed actions, and check password reset guidance when service resumes.
strings.records.atlink-beta.time: Updated 10/28 12:30 JST / Rechecked; no newly dated source update / Prior-source context; body not fully re-reviewed in this update
strings.records.railway-signups.title: Railway: 10/29 update keeps signups paused; reopening date unknown
strings.records.railway-signups.body: The 10/29 15:45 UTC status update keeps signups paused with no reopening date, prioritizing existing-customer reliability. About 100,000workspaces and at most 1.85% describe potential environment-variable exposure, not confirmed affected people.
strings.records.railway-signups.action: Revoke and reissue old secrets at their providers and audit usage. The next update scheduled for 10/30 at 16:00 UTC does not establish recovery at this cutoff.
strings.records.railway-signups.time: 10/30 00:45 JST status / Prior-source context; body not fully re-reviewed in this update
strings.records.studio-reporting.title: Studio: joint-report submissions planned for early 11
strings.records.studio-reporting.body: The update on the 28th at 00:30 says acceptance of joint reports to the Personal Information Protection Commission has not begun. Individual notification is not included in joint reporting. Reading of encryption keys and external accessibility were confirmed, but the number of records actually obtained remains undetermined.
strings.records.studio-reporting.action: Investigate actual use of form data and separately decide individual notification. Revoke external API keys with their issuers. Key rotation does not eliminate the possibility of earlier acquisition.
strings.records.studio-reporting.time: Updated 10/28 00:30 JST / Rechecked; no newly dated source update / Prior-source context; body not fully re-reviewed in this update

strings.records.connectwise-validation.body: The update on the 27th at 14:30 UTC says preparations for phased recovery are complete and required third-party validation is pending. It does not announce the start of restore access or full recovery. The recovery of Axcient Legacy Portal on the 22nd is a separate PHP mitigation matter.

strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.title: Tailscale: minimum fixed version 1.104.4 for 4 official advisories
strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.body: TS-2026-014–017 concern SSH Unix socket forwarding, SSH memory DoS, Serve Unix backends, and HTTP/2 capability confusion. The official bulletin specifies at least 1.104.4. A timing gap in changelog updates remains. Do not equate this with fixes for all 11 Tailworm items.
strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.action: Verify 1.104.4 or later on production clients and check SSH/Serve usage conditions. To temporarily disable SSH forwarding, set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and restart the daemon. Do not include headscale or experimental connectors in the same fix scope.
strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.time: Continued review of the 10/26 bulletin and 10/27 tag / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.title: Fireblocks mpc-lib: still no fix after assessment revision.
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.body: CERT VU701544 was revised on the 27th at 14:45 UTC. Descendant shares and chain codes may permit access to ancestor/root shares of the same MPC party, but this is not equivalent to obtaining a complete transfer key exceeding the threshold. Actual theft, amounts, and affected customer counts have not been disclosed.
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.action: Treat the fix as unavailable, protect chain codes as secrets, and investigate the entire hierarchy. Do not reuse Agent2.4.4 / SDK2.19.1 from the separate eMudhra incident as fixed versions for this vulnerability.
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.time: Revised 10/27 23:45 JST / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.fortinet-fips.title: Fortinet FIPS: 7.4 remediation build and inconsistent 7.2 notation
strings.records.fortinet-fips.body: The technical article dated the 27 announces availability of FIPS hardening builds. For 7.4, this is FIPS-CC-74-15 b9481. For 7.2, b9883 in the text differs from b9893 in the download path. Extended support for 7.0FIPS has ended, with no build planned this time.
strings.records.fortinet-fips.action: Match models and builds against official ReadMe files and support downloads. Do not automatically apply an ambiguous 7.2 number. Do not reuse the GA hardening table as individual minimum fixed versions for an unretrieved PSIRT advisory.
strings.records.fortinet-fips.time: 10/27 official update / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.tit: LiteLLM: revoke keys and rebuild environments after distribution-path compromise.
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.bod: Actual distribution of malicious 1.107.0 and containers was confirmed in the 10/21 incident. The attack-chain report on the 23rd explains the path from an unrevoked master key to publisher tokens and other access. Do not reuse victim counts from the separate March (month 3) incident here.
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.act: Check installation and execution paths during the affected period. Before simply updating pip packages, isolate and rebuild the environment and revoke/replace keys that were reachable. Product GHSA fixed versions in this window are separate from post-compromise safety checks.
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.tim: Continuing response to the 10/21 incident and 10/23 analysis / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.malware-packages.title: Malicious packages: separately check 27 GHSA malware-category advisories
strings.records.malware-packages.body: Includes trajmetrics0.5.3, numprint1.2.0, and @azure-growth/signup-ux-components1.2.2/1.2.3. Ranges below are as specified in GitHub advisories. Do not infer that all legitimate packages with similar names were compromised. Do not count 27 advisories as 27 newly affected organizations.
strings.records.malware-packages.action: Compare lockfiles and SBOMs with retrieval caches; do not verify suspicious artifacts by executing them. If installed or executed, isolate and rebuild the environment and revoke credentials that were reachable. Do not interpret an unspecified fixed version as meaning a safe version exists or that upgrading alone resolves the issue.
strings.records.malware-packages.time: Current GHSA publication window / malware classification / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.kev-linux-esx.title: KEV: Linux privilege escalation and missing ESX logging added
strings.records.kev-linux-esx.body: KEV version 2026.10.28 contains 1,762 entries. CVE-2026-46300 describes chaining with the 2 PHP flaws; forensicTriage is Yes and the deadline is 10/31. CVE-2026-41709 concerns actions left unlogged after administrator access, with a deadline of 11/11. Addition dates are not attack start dates; deadlines are requirements for US federal agencies.
strings.records.kev-linux-esx.action: Check kernel and embedded-product updates, including the running version after restart. Use the ESX vendor response matrix and treat missing logs as an investigation limitation.
strings.records.kev-linux-esx.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.php-kernel-identity.title: From PHP to the kernel and identity systems: observed artifacts and uncertainty
strings.records.php-kernel-identity.body: Dream’s report dated 10/26 describes artifacts of PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on 25 servers: 24 firewalls and an additional management server. It reports decrypted LDAP credentials and enumeration, but explicitly cannot determine whether password spraying, backdoor account creation or SAML key extraction succeeded. These are researcher observations without independent victim confirmation; direct evidence of AI code generation is also absent.
strings.records.php-kernel-identity.action: Restrict exposed management interfaces and update. Where compromise is suspected, investigate management servers, LDAP credentials, tunnels and identity logs. Do not infer undisclosed product names or affected versions.
strings.records.php-kernel-identity.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.sonet-disclosure.title: So-net: member information and some email passwords exposed
strings.records.sonet-disclosure.body: The official 10/27 notice says access on 10/19 was detected on 23 and disclosure established on 24. It separately reports 2,141,986 So-net member records and 443,495 plala (S course) member records. Passwords for member records are distinct from email passwords in some mail services: the latter were exposed and reset on 27. The notice also reports 16 bank-account records and 7 notification records. Do not add these as a count of people.
strings.records.sonet-disclosure.action: Reset affected email passwords using the official guidance and change reused passwords elsewhere. Do not infer exposure in other services such as NURO.
strings.records.sonet-disclosure.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.unm-recovery.title: UNM Health: clinical and academic recovery, with a warning about follow-on scams
strings.records.unm-recovery.body: The official 10/28 update reports fully functional clinical operations and resumed classes and research. Ambulance diversion and interrupted outpatient surgery and appointments on 10/26 remain recorded as real impacts. The institution says some end-user devices were affected without penetration of core systems or servers. Attacker claims of stolen data or payment offers are not confirmed disclosure or compensation.
strings.records.unm-recovery.action: Use official hospital channels to check rescheduled appointments. Do not engage with purported attackers or compensation offers.
strings.records.unm-recovery.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.silent-train.title: Silent Train: long-term monitoring of infrastructure serving communications, government and transport
strings.records.silent-train.body: Lumen Black Lotus Labs describes ephemeral relay chains tracked since 2023 and operations targeting management infrastructure. Victim notifications cover multiple years, rather than incidents newly occurring in this review. The report lists communications, government, defense, universities, water, energy and transport among targeted sectors without providing individual outage durations or financial losses.
strings.records.silent-train.action: Review exposed management interfaces, devices usable as relays and management-network telemetry. Do not rely solely on IP reputation.
strings.records.silent-train.time: 2026-10-28 / publication time unconfirmed / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.yamaha-nwr100.title: Yamaha NWR100: unauthenticated command execution and CONFIG access
strings.records.yamaha-nwr100.body: CVE-2026-97854 allows unauthenticated OS command execution, scored 9.8 in CVSS v3.1 and 9.3 in v4.0. CVE-2026-109822 concerns unauthenticated access to generated CONFIG files. Rev.26.00.07 and earlier are affected; Rev.26.00.08 is fixed. Potential impact is not a count of actual compromises.
strings.records.yamaha-nwr100.action: Update firmware. If delayed, restrict devices and source IP addresses allowed to access the Web GUI.
strings.records.yamaha-nwr100.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.yamaha-windows.title: Yamaha Windows products: separate installer and service-path fixes
strings.records.yamaha-windows.body: LAN Monitor installers through Ver.1.9.3 have a DLL-loading issue, fixed in Ver.1.10.1; already installed software itself is unaffected by this installer issue. YMS-VPN8 / YMS-VPN8-CP through Ver.1.04.00 have unquoted service paths, fixed in Ver.1.07.00. The latter requires permission to write to the system drive.
strings.records.yamaha-windows.action: Use the official fixed releases and avoid running installers beside untrusted DLLs. Review shared Windows access and write permissions.
strings.records.yamaha-windows.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.struts-anysetter.title: Struts REST: any-setter requires configuration as well as an update
strings.records.struts-anysetter.body: In Struts 2 versions 7.2.1–7.3.0, @StrutsParameter restrictions do not cover REST @JsonAnySetter members. JVN advises updating to 7.4.0 or later and using struts.rest.anySetter.requireAnnotations=true with @StrutsParameter(allowDynamicKeys = true). Conditions include REST use and any-setter declarations; this does not establish compromise of all Struts applications.
strings.records.struts-anysetter.action: Check the update, configuration and annotations together. Work around the issue by avoiding any-setter or validating values in the application before storage.
strings.records.struts-anysetter.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update
strings.records.edk2-pxe.title: EDK II: distinguish PXE exposure from shipped firmware fixes
strings.records.edk2-pxe.body: The official CVE-2026-97631 advisory describes pre-OS memory corruption by an attacker able to deliver ICMP errors during PXE boot. It identifies master as of 2026-09-14 and still lists Not patched currently. A fix PR does not prove a manufacturer has shipped a corrected BIOS or UEFI release.
strings.records.edk2-pxe.action: Disable unnecessary network boot and restrict PXE paths. Check firmware releases and deployment with the hardware supplier.
strings.records.edk2-pxe.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update

strings.records.dell-backup.body: DSA-2026-416 fixes command execution, authentication and other issues. The DD OS Feature line affects 7.7.1.0–8.8.0.0 and is remediated in 8.9.0.0 or later. strings.records.zip-rs-1030.body: Crafted ZIP files can escape the extraction directory through symlinks, bypass AES-entry HMAC checks at premature EOF, or terminate extraction through declared sizes. The escape needs knowledge of the destination path; legacy decoder issues require legacy-zip.

strings.records.soft-serve-1031.body: A race when making public repositories private can retain stale authorization and expose later commits. strings.records.soft-serve-1031.action: Upgrade to 0.12.3 or later. Restarting clears stale visibility but does not prevent recurrence; create new repositories private from the outset as an interim measure.

strings.records.lxd-authorization-1107.body: Cross-project instance and custom-volume copies check the destination without establishing permission to view the source. A separate DevLXD issue allows a guest with volume management enabled to read and write another guest’s volumes within the same project. These are different authorization boundaries.
strings.records.lxd-authorization-1107.action: Review copy permissions, source-project visibility and DevLXD volume-management settings. Restrict unnecessary guest permissions and investigate unexpected copies, device changes and secret access. Keep each advisory’s module boundary rather than reducing them to one release number.

strings.records.lxd-images-1107.body: 4 advisories cover image-hash validation order and rootfs, templates and exec-output symlinks. Importing attacker-influenced images or using a malicious image server and subsequent operations are prerequisites. File writes and possible command execution remain distinct, with different fix boundaries.
strings.records.lxd-images-1107.action: Restrict image sources and review import, instance file API and recorded-exec permissions. Apply each applicable fix and investigate hosts that used suspect images. A failed hash check does not prove that no write occurred.

strings.records.lxd-backups-1107.body: An authenticated user allowed to create storage volumes can reportedly stop the daemon with a backup lacking snapshot expiry. A separate advisory covers extra compression arguments leading to host writes and possible code execution. An earlier nil-check patch does not establish that adjacent fields were fixed.
strings.records.lxd-backups-1107.action: Restrict backup import and export permissions and inputs, and check the distinct fix boundaries below. Restarting the daemon is not a permanent fix; investigate potential host writes separately.

strings.records.lxd-ssrf-1107.body: An authenticated user with can_create_images can make requests to internal HTTP services from the daemon’s network position. The reported scope includes error-based port inference; hash validation blocks response-body retrieval. This does not establish full internal-data exfiltration.
strings.records.lxd-ssrf-1107.action: Restrict image-creation permissions, daemon egress and metadata reachability, and apply the official fix. Distinguish probing from response-body exfiltration when investigating logs.

strings.records.osac-1107.body: In remote or auto VM cluster mode, the attacker must be able to create or modify a labelled Secret in a namespace readable by the proxy. Its exec plugin runs with console-proxy pod privileges; the server URL is also an SSRF path. Local-only deployments are unaffected. The advisory names 0.0.4 while asking users to verify a release containing the patch.
strings.records.osac-1107.action: Restrict Secret writes in the relevant namespace and verify that the deployed image contains the fix. Pod execution does not establish host root; investigate service-account permissions, destinations and Secret changes.

strings.records.qiskit-qpy-version-anomaly-1109-: Qiskit SDK: QPY deserialization, C API out-of-bounds write and v2.6.2 table discrepancy

strings.records.rucio-auth-1113.title: Rucio: SSH challenges accepted as authentication tokens enable administrator impersonation
strings.records.rucio-auth-1113.body: SSH challenges are nonces for a later key exchange, but are stored alongside authentication tokens and not distinguished during validation. An unauthenticated caller can request a challenge for an arbitrary account and use it within its short lifetime to access APIs as that account, including an administrator. Exact affected and fixed branches are retained below.
strings.records.rucio-auth-1113.action: Update rucio to a fixed release on its branch: 35.9.1 / 38.6.1 / 40.4.2 / 41.1.1 or later. Review API exposure, authentication and privileged operations. Keep nonces separate from authenticated credentials.
strings.records.rails-imagemagick-1113.title: Active Storage: attachment alone can reach arbitrary file operations
strings.records.rails-imagemagick-1113.body: Applications accepting untrusted uploads with mini_magick processing and a policy that permits the relevant ImageMagick coders may allow arbitrary file writes merely by attaching an image. Disk service additionally exposes files readable by the process. Preview generation and an explicit analyze call are not prerequisites.
strings.records.rails-imagemagick-1113.action: Update activestorage to 8.0.5.2 / 8.1.4.1, check mini_magick >= 5.1 and the effective policy. Check that overrides such as MiniMagick.cli_env do not bypass it. For potentially exposed Disk service secrets, rotate/revoke secret_key_base, the master key and external tokens; do not retain exposed secrets as fallbacks.
strings.records.rails-web-1113.title: Rails: separate Strong Parameters, proxy-session and text-helper conditions
strings.records.rails-web-1113.body: The advisories cover each_key block return values passed to mass assignment, Live streaming denial of service, session disclosure in Active Storage proxy mode, Content-Type on GCS uploads, video analysis and text helpers. Using Rails alone does not establish every prerequisite.
strings.records.rails-web-1113.action: Verify resolved actionpack, actionview and activestorage versions at 8.0.5.2 / 8.1.4.1. Review custom code passing each_key return values into assignment, proxy/cache behavior, uploads and helpers against each advisory.
strings.records.aspire-dashboard-1113.title: Aspire: an unauthenticated NotFound route is not fixed by a runtime update
strings.records.aspire-dashboard-1113.body: The Aspire Dashboard NotFound route may allow unauthenticated telemetry deletion. Standalone browser-token deployments may also disclose the browser token; AppHost-hosted dashboards are affected too. Releases 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 are not fixed, and a .NET runtime/SDK update does not replace the Dashboard.
strings.records.aspire-dashboard-1113.action: Update Dashboard to 13.6.5 or later. Replace container images and existing deployment manifests and redeploy. Check resolved Dashboard SDK packages, CLI bundles or custom paths selected by AppHost, then restart. A package-reference edit alone does not establish the running version.
strings.records.hono-routing-1113.title: Hono: mount and router path differences can bypass authentication middleware
strings.records.hono-routing-1113.body: Mount-prefix removal, re-normalization and RegExpRouter wildcard matching may reach inner handlers without the outer authentication middleware. Separate text/ping CSRF, multipart form validation and css-helper advisories retain their version details below.
strings.records.hono-routing-1113.action: Update hono to 4.13.16. Authenticate inside the mounted application; consider the documented TrieRouter workaround where needed. Regenerate PreparedRegExpRouter data and check custom patterns now rejected by the fixed router.
strings.records.hono-node-1113.title: Hono Node adapter: proxy/application path disagreement and WebSocket DoS
strings.records.hono-node-1113.body: A proxy may keep raw backslashes while the Node adapter normalizes them into separators, bypassing proxy path controls. This does not disable in-application authentication on the rewritten path. An ECONNRESET during asynchronous WebSocket upgrade is a separate process-crash issue.
strings.records.hono-node-1113.action: Check branch-specific @hono/node-server fixes: 1.19.18 / 2.1.6 for paths and 2.1.6 for the WebSocket issue. Verify proxy and application authentication. Updating core hono does not by itself update the adapter.
strings.records.pgedge-rag-1113.title: pgEdge RAG: ordinary concurrent queries can mix results across tenants
strings.records.pgedge-rag-1113.body: A shared BM25 index clears, populates and searches under separate locks, so ordinary concurrent unauthenticated queries can return another tenant’s documents. No injection or malformed input is needed. Separate advisories cover unbounded corpus reads and provider-key fragments in errors.
strings.records.pgedge-rag-1113.action: Upgrade the RAG Server product release to 2.0.0 or later. Go module first_patched_version values identify commits through pseudo-versions and differ from product releases. hybrid_enabled: false temporarily bypasses the shared index. The server’s own logs cannot retrospectively identify affected responses; rotate exposed provider credentials.
strings.records.pgedge-llm-1113.title: pgEdge Go LLM: health-endpoint errors disclose provider-key fragments
strings.records.pgedge-llm-1113.body: The bundled HTTP proxy permits access when no Authorize hook is set, and its health handler returns provider errors containing key fragments. The advisory names affected releases 0.1.0 / 0.1.1 and explicitly says the previously cited product release 0.1.2 does not exist.
strings.records.pgedge-llm-1113.action: Upgrade the product release to 0.2.0 or later and rotate exposed provider credentials. Distinguish the table’s Go pseudo-version from a product release. Configure an Authorize hook and restrict access to the listening port.
strings.records.pgedge-control-1113.title: pgEdge Control Plane: trust authentication in generated pg_hba.conf
strings.records.pgedge-control-1113.body: Generated pg_hba.conf includes trust authentication for local and loopback connections. Do not equate a process that can connect with an authenticated database user; inspect existing generated configuration and access paths.
strings.records.pgedge-control-1113.action: Update Control Plane to 0.11.0 and follow the advisory when checking existing pg_hba.conf and local/loopback access. Updating management software alone does not establish that existing database configuration is corrected.
strings.records.pillow-tiff-1113.title: Pillow: pixel-count limits do not bound metadata processing
strings.records.pillow-tiff-1113.body: Overlapping TIFF/EXIF tag reads can make a small file consume excessive memory even with a tiny declared pixel count. A separate libtiff save issue lets metadata geometry disagree with the real image buffer, allowing memory reads/corruption and crashes.
strings.records.pillow-tiff-1113.action: Update Pillow to 13.0.0. Review TIFF saves, inherited exif/tiffinfo, Image.open and getexif paths, and bound worker memory/time. MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS alone does not prevent metadata-driven denial of service.
strings.records.soupsieve-selectors-1113.title: Soup Sieve: selector processing on untrusted HTML has complexity risks
strings.records.soupsieve-selectors-1113.body: Descendant combinators and general sibling combinators inside :has() have separate advisories and different fixed versions. Check workload conditions for services processing untrusted HTML or selectors.

strings.records.grpc-xds-1113.title: gRPC xDS: safe_regex and route-level RBAC application differ

strings.records.ruby-msgpack-1113.title: MessagePack Ruby: JRuby decoder header counts can exhaust memory

strings.records.addressable-uri-1113.title: Addressable: separate display hosts, path normalization and template DoS

strings.records.astro-slots-1113.title: Astro: reflected XSS through slot names in Solid/Svelte integrations
strings.records.astro-slots-1113.body: Unescaped slot names can cause reflected XSS in @astrojs/solid-js and @astrojs/svelte. Check the integration packages independently.
strings.records.astro-slots-1113.action: Check @astrojs/solid-js at 7.1.2 and @astrojs/svelte at 9.1.2. Updating Astro core alone does not establish that its integrations are fixed.
strings.records.basic-ftp-1113.title: basic-ftp: process crashes from CR/LF and MLSD parsing
strings.records.basic-ftp-1113.body: CR/LF in passwords or resumed-download paths and an MLSD __proto__ fact trigger separate unhandled-exception paths. Release 6.2.3 fixes the former but remains affected by the latter.
strings.records.basic-ftp-1113.action: Update basic-ftp to 6.2.4. Review untrusted FTP listings and input handling; 6.2.3 alone does not fix both issues.
strings.records.signalk-logs-1113.title: Signal K: unauthenticated WebSockets can subscribe to buffered logs
strings.records.signalk-logs-1113.body: WebSockets intentionally allow pre-login connections, but log subscriptions omit the authorization checks used elsewhere and can replay buffered server logs. The advisory describes code review, not captured frames from a running server.
strings.records.signalk-logs-1113.action: Check the signalk-server fix in 2.31.0-beta.1 and its availability in the stable release you use. Review WebSocket exposure and sensitive information in logs.
strings.records.sharp-backend-1113.title: code16/sharp: autocomplete SSRF and embed_key class instantiation
strings.records.sharp-backend-1113.body: The advisories separately cover an unanchored autocomplete endpoint regex and arbitrary class instantiation through embed_key. Check access permissions and outbound connectivity for the CMS administration features.
strings.records.sharp-backend-1113.action: Check code16/sharp fixes at 9.23.0 / 10.0.0-beta.4 for the applicable branch. Review autocomplete destinations and embed API permissions.

strings.records.screenconnect-response-1113.titl: ScreenConnect: separate technician-client protection from compromise remediation
strings.records.screenconnect-response-1113.body: ConnectWise’s 11/12 18:45 UTC update identifies approximately 400 environments with RMM+ extensions for precautionary action, not confirmed compromises. Its current assessment finds no evidence of compromised ConnectWise infrastructure or a ScreenConnect vulnerability in initial access. Clients at 26.6.5 or later block the SCKit endpoint-to-technician spread technique, but do not remove existing compromises.
strings.records.screenconnect-response-1113.acti: Verify the installed client on every technician workstation is 26.6.5 or later; keep the identified extensions disabled. Revoke web/IdP sessions from a trusted device and investigate with independent EDR or other out-of-band tooling. Preserve evidence, then clear queued commands/Toolbox items, unauthorized clients and persistence; validate before reconnecting.
strings.records.air-terminal6-1113.title: Air Terminal 6: OS command injection requires management login
strings.records.air-terminal6-1113.body: JVN published this on 11/12. On v1.01.80 and earlier, a user able to log in to the web administration interface can execute commands as root. This is not an unauthenticated Internet-wide condition. The developer says fixed firmware has been deployed and disconnected devices update automatically on reconnection, so no user action is required.
strings.records.air-terminal6-1113.action: Check the official automatic-update conditions and device connectivity. Do not invent a fixed firmware number, which JVN does not list. Limit unnecessary management-interface access and shared credentials.
strings.records.kusanagi-nginx-1113.title: KUSANAGI: the 11/12 revision clarifies Nginx redirect scope
strings.records.kusanagi-nginx-1113.body: JVN published on 11/09 and revised affected scope on 11/12. CRLF handling in WordPress Nginx redirect rules can inject response headers when a crafted URL is visited. Affected: all KUSANAGI 7; all 8 Free/Business/Premium; 9 Security/Enterprise through 10.7.2-1 and Free/Business/Premium through 9.12.2-1. Apache httpd configurations are excluded.
strings.records.kusanagi-nginx-1113.action: Check the edition and Nginx configuration, then apply the developer’s latest update or official workaround. Keep Apache exclusions explicit and do not infer a minimum fixed version absent from JVN.
strings.records.apache-httpd-1113.title: Apache HTTP Server: verify release 2.4.71 and deployed binaries
strings.records.apache-httpd-1113.body: JVN’s 11/12 notice announces Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 for multiple issues in the 2.4 series. JVN delegates details to Apache advisories; this short notice alone does not establish every CVE prerequisite or exploitation status.
strings.records.apache-httpd-1113.action: Check official Apache advisories and distribution backports against enabled modules and running binaries. Distinguish an available update from the process running after restart.
strings.records.apache-httpd-1113.time: 11/12 JVN publication / notice of Apache 11/11 update

records.action: Keep affected connections disabled and await individual resumption guidance. Do not generalize the statement that there are no signs of compromise of encrypted backup archives into a claim that every Microsoft365 tenant is uncompromised.
records.time: Updated 10/27 23:30 JST / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: Tailscale: minimum fixed version 1.104.4 for 4 official advisories
records.body: TS-2026-014–017 concern SSH Unix socket forwarding, SSH memory DoS, Serve Unix backends, and HTTP/2 capability confusion. The official bulletin specifies at least 1.104.4. A timing gap in changelog updates remains. Do not equate this with fixes for all 11 Tailworm items.
records.action: Verify 1.104.4 or later on production clients and check SSH/Serve usage conditions. To temporarily disable SSH forwarding, set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and restart the daemon. Do not include headscale or experimental connectors in the same fix scope.
records.time: Continued review of the 10/26 bulletin and 10/27 tag / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: Fireblocks mpc-lib: still no fix after assessment revision.
records.body: CERT VU701544 was revised on the 27th at 14:45 UTC. Descendant shares and chain codes may permit access to ancestor/root shares of the same MPC party, but this is not equivalent to obtaining a complete transfer key exceeding the threshold. Actual theft, amounts, and affected customer counts have not been disclosed.
records.action: Treat the fix as unavailable, protect chain codes as secrets, and investigate the entire hierarchy. Do not reuse Agent2.4.4 / SDK2.19.1 from the separate eMudhra incident as fixed versions for this vulnerability.
records.time: Revised 10/27 23:45 JST / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: Fortinet FIPS: 7.4 remediation build and inconsistent 7.2 notation
records.body: The technical article dated the 27 announces availability of FIPS hardening builds. For 7.4, this is FIPS-CC-74-15 b9481. For 7.2, b9883 in the text differs from b9893 in the download path. Extended support for 7.0FIPS has ended, with no build planned this time.
records.action: Match models and builds against official ReadMe files and support downloads. Do not automatically apply an ambiguous 7.2 number. Do not reuse the GA hardening table as individual minimum fixed versions for an unretrieved PSIRT advisory.
records.time: 10/27 official update / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: LiteLLM: revoke keys and rebuild environments after distribution-path compromise.
records.body: Actual distribution of malicious 1.107.0 and containers was confirmed in the 10/21 incident. The attack-chain report on the 23rd explains the path from an unrevoked master key to publisher tokens and other access. Do not reuse victim counts from the separate March (month 3) incident here.
records.action: Check installation and execution paths during the affected period. Before simply updating pip packages, isolate and rebuild the environment and revoke/replace keys that were reachable. Product GHSA fixed versions in this window are separate from post-compromise safety checks.
records.time: Continuing response to the 10/21 incident and 10/23 analysis / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: Malicious packages: separately check 27 GHSA malware-category advisories
records.body: Includes trajmetrics0.5.3, numprint1.2.0, and @azure-growth/signup-ux-components1.2.2/1.2.3. Ranges below are as specified in GitHub advisories. Do not infer that all legitimate packages with similar names were compromised. Do not count 27 advisories as 27 newly affected organizations.
records.action: Compare lockfiles and SBOMs with retrieval caches; do not verify suspicious artifacts by executing them. If installed or executed, isolate and rebuild the environment and revoke credentials that were reachable. Do not interpret an unspecified fixed version as meaning a safe version exists or that upgrading alone resolves the issue.

records.title: KEV: Linux privilege escalation and missing ESX logging added
records.body: KEV version 2026.10.28 contains 1,762 entries. CVE-2026-46300 describes chaining with the 2 PHP flaws; forensicTriage is Yes and the deadline is 10/31. CVE-2026-41709 concerns actions left unlogged after administrator access, with a deadline of 11/11. Addition dates are not attack start dates; deadlines are requirements for US federal agencies.
records.action: Check kernel and embedded-product updates, including the running version after restart. Use the ESX vendor response matrix and treat missing logs as an investigation limitation.
records.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: From PHP to the kernel and identity systems: observed artifacts and uncertainty
records.body: Dream’s report dated 10/26 describes artifacts of PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on 25 servers: 24 firewalls and an additional management server. It reports decrypted LDAP credentials and enumeration, but explicitly cannot determine whether password spraying, backdoor account creation or SAML key extraction succeeded. These are researcher observations without independent victim confirmation; direct evidence of AI code generation is also absent.
records.action: Restrict exposed management interfaces and update. Where compromise is suspected, investigate management servers, LDAP credentials, tunnels and identity logs. Do not infer undisclosed product names or affected versions.
records.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: So-net: member information and some email passwords exposed
records.body: The official 10/27 notice says access on 10/19 was detected on 23 and disclosure established on 24. It separately reports 2,141,986 So-net member records and 443,495 plala (S course) member records. Passwords for member records are distinct from email passwords in some mail services: the latter were exposed and reset on 27. The notice also reports 16 bank-account records and 7 notification records. Do not add these as a count of people.
records.action: Reset affected email passwords using the official guidance and change reused passwords elsewhere. Do not infer exposure in other services such as NURO.
records.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: UNM Health: clinical and academic recovery, with a warning about follow-on scams
records.body: The official 10/28 update reports fully functional clinical operations and resumed classes and research. Ambulance diversion and interrupted outpatient surgery and appointments on 10/26 remain recorded as real impacts. The institution says some end-user devices were affected without penetration of core systems or servers. Attacker claims of stolen data or payment offers are not confirmed disclosure or compensation.
records.action: Use official hospital channels to check rescheduled appointments. Do not engage with purported attackers or compensation offers.
records.time: 2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update

records.title: Silent Train: long-term monitoring of infrastructure serving communications, government and transport
records.body: Lumen Black Lotus Labs describes ephemeral relay chains tracked since 2023 and operations targeting management infrastructure. Victim notifications cover multiple years, rather than incidents newly occurring in this review. The report lists communications, government, defense, universities, water, energy and transport among targeted sectors without providing individual outage durations or financial losses.
records.action: Review exposed management interfaces, devices usable as relays and management-network telemetry. Do not rely solely on IP reputation.

records.title: Yamaha NWR100: unauthenticated command execution and CONFIG access
records.body: CVE-2026-97854 allows unauthenticated OS command execution, scored 9.8 in CVSS v3.1 and 9.3 in v4.0. CVE-2026-109822 concerns unauthenticated access to generated CONFIG files. Rev.26.00.07 and earlier are affected; Rev.26.00.08 is fixed. Potential impact is not a count of actual compromises.
records.action: Update firmware. If delayed, restrict devices and source IP addresses allowed to access the Web GUI.

records.title: Yamaha Windows products: separate installer and service-path fixes
records.body: LAN Monitor installers through Ver.1.9.3 have a DLL-loading issue, fixed in Ver.1.10.1; already installed software itself is unaffected by this installer issue. YMS-VPN8 / YMS-VPN8-CP through Ver.1.04.00 have unquoted service paths, fixed in Ver.1.07.00. The latter requires permission to write to the system drive.

records.title: Struts REST: any-setter requires configuration as well as an update
records.body: In Struts 2 versions 7.2.1–7.3.0, @StrutsParameter restrictions do not cover REST @JsonAnySetter members. JVN advises updating to 7.4.0 or later and using struts.rest.anySetter.requireAnnotations=true with @StrutsParameter(allowDynamicKeys = true). Conditions include REST use and any-setter declarations; this does not establish compromise of all Struts applications.
records.action: Check the update, configuration and annotations together. Work around the issue by avoiding any-setter or validating values in the application before storage.

By contrast, CVE-2026-124445 (OneTimeAuth token replay and PIN brute force from 7.0.1 before 8.4.0) and CVE-2026-124467 (chained RCE via ESign router LFI and fax upload before 8.4.0) are fixed in 8.4.0. Updating only to 8.3.0 does not resolve the issues fixed in 8.4.0. Initial GitHub advisory publication occurred in months 8 and 9.
records.action: Verify a release at 8.4.0 or later and do not conflate 8.3.0 fixes with 8.4.0 fixes. Check whether the fax/sms and ESign modules are enabled, and investigate suspicious access to sqlconf.php, temporary upload paths and patient-portal token usage.

records.title: Kyverno: cross-namespace boundary bypass via apiCall and variable generate targets
records.body: In CVE-2026-124440 (from 1.19.1 before 1.19.2), malformed percent-encoding bypasses the apiCall namespace clamp and allows calling cross-namespace or cluster-scoped APIs with the admission-controller ServiceAccount privileges. In CVE-2026-124441 (before 1.19.2), templating the generate rule's kind and namespace with variables skips authorization checks and allows creating resources in arbitrary namespaces via the background-controller. Both require permissions to create a Policy within a namespace.
records.action: Update to 1.19.2 and audit delegated namespaced Policy creation permissions, Policies using apiCall or variable generate rules, and creation history for unexpected MutatingWebhooks or RoleBindings.

records.title: Craft CMS: out-of-scope GraphQL reads and control-panel signing oracle
records.body: In CVE-2026-124427 (from 5.0.0 before 5.11.2), public GraphQL schemas or scoped tokens can traverse prev/next fields to read entries from out-of-scope sections. In CVE-2026-124430 (from 5.10.0 before 5.11.2), non-administrator control-panel users can obtain HMAC-signed Twig templates from app/render-elements and achieve code execution via the login redirect. Keep unauthenticated GraphQL prerequisites distinct from control-panel privilege prerequisites.
records.action: Update to 5.11.2. Review public GraphQL schema availability and token scopes, non-administrator control-panel permissions, and request logs for app/render-elements.

records.title: imgproxy: ICO loader integer overflow and staged fixes across 4.0.16 / 4.0.17
records.body: CVE-2026-123614 affects 4.0.0 before 4.0.16, where an ICO data_size integer overflow causes heap corruption and RCE, fixed in 4.0.16. records.title: Hickory DNS: DNSSEC validation bypass and unpatched legacy hickory-proto range

records.action: Update hickory-net to 0.26.2 or later. Note explicitly that legacy hickory-proto 0.1 through 0.25.0-alpha.3 has no in-series fixed release and requires migrating to hickory-net 0.26.2 or later; review dependency trees that rely on DNSSEC validation.

records.body: JVN published on 11/09 and revised affected scope on 11/12. CRLF handling in WordPress Nginx redirect rules can inject response headers when a crafted URL is visited. Affected: all KUSANAGI 7; all 8 Free/Business/Premium; 9 Security/Enterprise through 10.7.2-1 and Free/Business/Premium through 9.12.2-1. Apache httpd configurations are excluded.
records.action: Check the edition and Nginx configuration, then apply the developer’s latest update or official workaround. Keep Apache exclusions explicit and do not infer a minimum fixed version absent from JVN.
records.time: 11/12 affected-scope revision / first published 11/09

records.title: Apache HTTP Server: verify release 2.4.71 and deployed binaries
records.body: JVN’s 11/12 notice announces Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 for multiple issues in the 2.4 series. JVN delegates details to Apache advisories; this short notice alone does not establish every CVE prerequisite or exploitation status.
records.action: Check official Apache advisories and distribution backports against enabled modules and running binaries. Distinguish an available update from the process running after restart.
records.time: 11/12 JVN publication / notice of Apache 11/11 update
